lines.cd1: A check digit is the final digit of a code. It is calculated from all the other digits.
lines.cd2: It is used on barcodes, book numbers, vehicle identification numbers, and credit cards.
lines.me1: The method: multiply each digit by its position, add the totals, and divide by ten. The remainder is the check digit.
lines.we1: Take the code nine four five three four four. Multiply and add: nine, eight, fifteen, twelve, twenty. The total is sixty four.
lines.we2: Sixty four divided by ten leaves a remainder of four. That matches the last digit, so the code is accepted.
lines.pr1: Now try three five two one three two. Multiply and add: three, ten, six, four, fifteen. The total is thirty eight, and the remainder is eight.
lines.pr2: The last digit is two, not eight, so the code is rejected.
lines.outro: Multiply by position, add, divide by ten. Compare the remainder with the check digit.
